key_contribution: A cognitive-inspired compositional FSCIL method that represents each class as a set of N primitive prototypes (image patches), uses linear CKA similarity to compute composition scores between input patch features and class primitive sets, and introduces a primitive reuse module with cross-class attention to enhance reusability, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy with the least catastrophic forgetting on three benchmarks while providing interpretable class compositions.
limitations: The method neglects many-shot scenarios where the update of primitives cannot be ignored, as explicitly stated in the Impact Statement. Additionally, the performance gains over strong baselines (CLOM, NC-FSCIL) are modest (~1.5–2% in last-session accuracy), and the evaluation is limited to 5-shot settings on three datasets, leaving open whether the compositional structure offers scaling advantages with more sessions or larger class counts.
surprise_factor: No particularly surprising findings — the CKA repurposing is a clever but natural adaptation, and the performance improvements over SOTA are consistent yet modest (1.5–2% on last-session accuracy). The interpretability visualizations are appealing but qualitative, and the robustness advantage of CKA over DeepEMD/FRN under noisy features, while demonstrated, follows from the simpler local-computation structure rather than revealing an unexpected phenomenon.

title: BiE: Bi-Exponent Block Floating-Point for Large Language Models Quantization

builds_on.title: Revisiting Block-based Quantisation: What is Important for Sub-8-bit LLM Inference?
builds_on.evidence: Paper states 'Building upon the vanilla BFP, BiE uses a bi-shared exponent, one for the normal values part and the other for the outlier values part' — directly extends the BFP format with a second shared exponent.

compares_to.title: Smoothquant: Accurate and efficient post-training quantization for large language models
compares_to.evidence: Listed in Tables 2, 3, 5, 6, and 8 as SmoothQuant W8A8 and W6A6 baselines with perplexity and accuracy numbers alongside BiE results.

compares_to.title: Revisiting Block-based Quantisation: What is Important for Sub-8-bit LLM Inference?
compares_to.evidence: Listed in Tables 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 as BFP W4A4 and W3A3 baselines with perplexity and accuracy numbers alongside BiE results.

key_contribution: Proposes Bi-Exponent Block Floating-Point (BiE), a novel low-bit numerical representation that uses two per-block shared exponents (one for normal values, one for outliers) to natively handle the superposition of distributions in LLM activations, combined with a Bayesian Optimization-based offline threshold search, achieving near-lossless 4-bit quantization (matching 8-bit SmoothQuant) with 3.51× hardware throughput over FP16 on FPGA.
limitations: Evaluation is limited to OPT and LLaMA-2 model families, and the per-tensor threshold granularity with offline-only optimization may not generalize to architectures with different outlier patterns (e.g., Mistral, Gemma). At 3-bit on large models (OPT-66B perplexity 32.41), substantial accuracy degradation remains, and hardware validation is restricted to FPGA simulation rather than production GPU/ASIC deployment.
surprise_factor: The most notable result is that BiE W4A4 on OPT-66B achieves 9.82 WikiText2 perplexity, nearly matching FP16 (9.12) and SmoothQuant W8A8 (9.62), while vanilla BFP W4A4 degrades to 14.16 — a large gap that validates the bi-exponent design for outlier-heavy models. However, this is a well-motivated extension of BFP with clear theoretical grounding (Equation 7 error analysis), so the result is more confirmatory than surprising. The 3-bit case on OPT-66B (32.41) still shows the approach has limits at extreme low bits.

title: Active Statistical Inference
task_novelty_note: Extends statistical inference (confidence intervals, hypothesis tests) from the i.i.d. / uniform-sampling setting of PPI to the adaptive, ML-guided label-collection setting.

builds_on.title: Prediction-powered inference
builds_on.evidence: Paper states 'PPI can be seen as a special case of our methodology' and the active estimator reduces to the PPI estimator under uniform sampling; the AIPW-based estimator structure is directly inherited from PPI.

builds_on.title: Estimation of regression coefficients when some regressors are not always observed
builds_on.evidence: Paper states the active mean estimator 'is essentially the augmented inverse propensity weighting (AIPW) estimator (Robins et al., 1994), with a particular choice of propensities based on the certainty of the machine learning model.'

compares_to.title: Prediction-powered inference
compares_to.evidence: Compared as the 'uniform' baseline in all experiments (Figures 1-4); paper states 'The first baseline replaces active sampling with the uniformly random sampling rule and corresponds to prediction-powered inference (PPI) (Angelopoulos et al., 2023a).'

key_contribution: A methodology for valid statistical inference (confidence intervals and hypothesis tests) that uses a machine learning model's uncertainty to strategically select which data points to label, achieving the same inferential accuracy with over 80% fewer labels than classical methods and 20–60% fewer than prediction-powered inference, while maintaining provable coverage guarantees for any convex M-estimation target.
limitations: The method relies on the i.i.d. assumption for data points, which may be violated in sequential collection settings, and if the model's uncertainty estimates are miscalibrated, active inference can underperform both classical inference and PPI.
surprise_factor: The 80%+ budget savings over classical inference is largely predicted by the variance decomposition and is not deeply surprising; the more notable empirical finding is the consistent 20–25% gain over the stronger PPI baseline across three diverse domains, suggesting that adaptive collection captures a real but bounded increment beyond what ML predictions alone provide. The practical caveat that active inference with a poorly trained model (no fine-tuning) can underperform PPI is a useful negative result that tempers the method's appeal in low-data regimes.
